I would have given them 1 star but I have had many tires patched in the past properly, this time I had tires pulled off my wheel and mounted on new ones and balanced. When I called I told the guy what I wanted and he quoted me $120. Upon arrival I was told $160 because of the sensors, I told them I just wanted normal valve stems and the guy helping me called over the older man they called maestro. He said $140. While they were talking, I grabbed some valve stems from a repair kit and he still wanted to charge me $140.

Then, I had forgotten I needed new acorn style lugs but the thin profile for my new wheels. I went to get the lugs quickly and returned and was told they were too thin. He then gave me a different acorn that was thicker and sent me back for new lugs. Against my better judgement I grabbed new ones and then they ok’ed them. When it came time to put the lugs on, they realized the keyed socket wouldn’t fit and maestro tried to tell me that the old ones were the proper lugs. When installing the guy let the impact just crack them down. I knew immediately it was incorrect and ordered the proper lugs from the wheel manufacturer. service_quality_in_session.snippet:
I recently drove to this shop to have my tire checked because I had noticed a screw in it. Unfortunately, my experience left me questioning both the quality of the work and the honesty of the service.

When I arrived, the employee pointed out the screw, but instead of removing it first to confirm whether it had actually punctured through, he immediately began working to put the tire back on the rim. Only after that did he submerge the tire in the water tank—something that should have been done first to properly identify any leaks.

After leaving the shop, while driving with the window down, I heard a repetitive noise from the tire — a clear sign that something was still lodged in it. I pulled over and found the same screw still in place, the very reason I had come in. What’s more concerning is that even if there had been more than one screw or nail, the employee never bothered to pull them all out and verify they were properly handled. That shows a lack of thoroughness and doesn’t build trust with customers.

In addition, the employee who handled my service (the one wearing sunglasses) did not seem very careful when lifting my vehicle, as he didn’t check for the proper lift points. His overall approach felt rushed and inattentive.

While the repair only cost $15, customers deserve honesty and proper service no matter the price. My advice to future visitors is to be cautious, double-check the work before leaving, and if you deal with the employee wearing sunglasses, make sure his work is reviewed. When customers pay for service, they should leave confident and satisfied, not worried.
service_quality_in_session.reasoning: Employee skipped proper steps; approach was rushed and inattentive.

My husband and I were the first guests to arrive for the Valentine’s Day special event. We booked this experience specifically because the event was advertised as including unlimited drinks and a live performance by SWV.

The advertisement felt misleading, and it was unfair to collect payment under one promise and deliver something entirely different.

The discussion escalated unnecessarily, as the owner began arguing with both myself and another guest regarding the advertisement. Following that exchange, service noticeably declined. Drinks and appetizers took an excessive amount of time to arrive. As more guests arrived, many voiced similar frustrations regarding the misleading promotion.

The entire evening felt chaotic and uncomfortable. Some guests did not receive their food at all and were told the restaurant had run out of salmon, which was listed as a featured entrée. However, approximately 45 minutes later, I personally observed a server delivering a salmon entrée to another table.

Overall, this was not the romantic, organized Valentine’s experience that was advertised or expected. We left feeling extremely disappointed. This is not a venue we would recommend for a special occasion, particularly one as meaningful as Valentine’s Day.

calls_unanswered.snippet:
I purchased my car from Auto City over 9 months ago and have always been a loyal customer who pays on time and maintains full coverage insurance. When I bought the car, I provided my insurance policy, which was accepted without issue.
Six months later, when it came time to re-verify coverage, nothing had changed on my policy. However, the dealership suddenly refused to accept it, claiming that having an excluded driver (my husband) on the policy was no longer acceptable—even though they had previously approved it. They told me I would either need to remove him (which my insurance company cannot do), downgrade to liability, or purchase their own COI insurance in addition to my full coverage. I was not willing to downgrade my personal insurance.

During this dispute, I attempted to make my car payments, but the dealership refused to accept them online. They added the insurance fee to my payment portal, preventing me from paying my actual car payment unless I included their insurance fee. This forced me to call in and pay over the phone, which was both frustrating and unfair. At one point, they even refused to take my payment over the phone until I agreed to purchase their insurance. Because I pushed back, I fell behind a month, and they repossessed my car—claiming “no insurance” and “non-payment of the car note.”

The most discouraging part was my conversation with General Manager Sarah Arellano. She stated that the reason my husband could not be on my insurance policy was because he was a “risk.” I explained that she is not an insurance professional, does not have his driving information, and has no authority to make that determination. Despite my efforts to resolve the issue, including my insurance company reaching out directly to her, calls went unanswered or were made outside of business hours.

When I asked what I could do to get my car back, I was told they no longer wanted to do business with me. After faithfully paying for over 9 months without ever being late, I was denied the opportunity to continue.

This experience shows a lack of consistency, transparency, and respect for customers. I believe leadership should act in the best interest of the company, not based on personal feelings. Unfortunately, this dealership’s practices are misleading and unfair.

Do not purchase from this dealership.
calls_unanswered.reasoning: Customer and insurer's calls to the GM went unanswered.

When asked if I could look at the part to ensure it was the right one, they said I had to hork up the money for the transmission before I could see it.  Entire thing seems like a scam, and I will be buying parts for my transmission swap project elsewhere.

Edit:
What I was calling about was getting more information about a transmission I'm looking for since their system lists the Subaru WRX STI and Subaru WRX as the same vehicle.  It's also ambiguous if a transmission listed is the WRX STI manual, WRX manual, or WRX CVT.  These three are very easy to tell apart with a couple of pictures of the front of the bell housing and the rear of the transmission, and of the three, the WRX STI manual is the only one that is capable of having 700-800 HP pushed through it.  If they had the transmission, that would have opened up the discussion to also getting the driveshaft, axels, and rear diff.

However, instead of addressing issues brought up by the problematic interaction, the owner shows the quality of their character by using personal attacks.  This is not a business operating in good faith and you should take your business elsewhere.  This review was written as a warning to others to avoid this business like the plague.

frontline_communication.snippet: The body work done on my car was satisfactory, not great,  but the communications and updates were lacking. I was told that I would receive regular updates via text by my advisor, Andrew. After a week of no communications I called to ensure they had my correct contact information. After my call, I received a text update that I called for status. Over the 30 days, I reached out a total of 3 times to request an update. The last update, I was told by Andrew that my car would be ready for pickup the next day, unless I heard otherwise from him. I didn't hear otherwise, and I knew they closed at 6pm, so I showed up at 5pm the next day as promised. Andrew meets me in the lobby and said they can't release the car to me on the day it was promised.  I was furious at this point.  So I get in my rental car that was overdue to be returned and drove home. The minute I get home, a peer of Andrew's calls to say that I can come pick up my car.

frontline_communication.snippet:

followup_dropped.snippet:
In November 2024, I paid $1,100 for a Viper alarm and Kenwood stereo installation. Within a month, I returned for wiring shorts, and four months later, I returned again for alarm reprogramming and wire adjustments.

By January 2026, the alarm wiring shorted and drained the battery, leaving the truck undrivable. I spoke with Mazin, who insisted I bring the vehicle in despite it being dead. A technician called me back to suggest a mobile inspection but never followed up.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
Review for 2015 Chevy Tahoe Transmission Service (Terrell & Dallas Locations)
I’ve been dealing with transmission issues on my 2015 Chevy Tahoe since 2021, when I first had the transmission replaced. Over the past 4 years, my truck has been in and out of the shop more than 20 times, each visit lasting 2 to 4 weeks. Despite all this, the transmission continued to slip while stopped and shift hard from 3rd to 2nd gear.
I was repeatedly told:

The torque converter was bad—it’s been replaced over 10 times.
The issue was due to bad mechanics, but I was assured a new tech would resolve it.
I dealt with 4 different individuals and multiple techs across both locations.

Three weeks ago, I dropped my truck off again and spoke with the person I’ve been working with for the past two years. After a week, I was told my vehicle had not been serviced properly under warranty. I was shocked—how could that be after so many visits and torque converter replacements? I was told it didn’t matter. After a 30-minute discussion, he agreed to fix the issue but said he wouldn’t make money from the repair and asked me to help pay. I refused, and he finally agreed to fix it—but said my warranty would be void.
I picked up my truck this past Saturday. I was told a mechanic would ride with me to confirm the fix—that didn’t happen. Then I was hit with a $510 charge for the TCM, which apparently wasn’t covered by the warranty. I asked to speak to the owner multiple times and was refused. I was told, “Don’t contact us again.”
To top it off, every time I picked up my truck, it was returned with an empty gas tank—even this last time. When I asked about it, I was told, “How did you think cars drive? They need gas.” Unbelievable.
I have messages and written statements backing up everything I’ve said, including one that reads:

“Wow, you’ve been very patient with us. I would probably handle things differently if I were in your shoes.”

I’ve tried to be respectful and patient. All I ever wanted was a properly functioning transmission—not 4 years of frustration and financial burden.
I wonder if the owner will reach out to discuss, if not.. oh well.. lesson learned from me.  Even though I was treated like trash, I won't lower my standards and mention all names that were involved.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Unexpected charge after being assured warranty coverage; classic bait-and-switch.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Review for 2015 Chevy Tahoe Transmission Service (Terrell & Dallas Locations)
I’ve been dealing with transmission issues on my 2015 Chevy Tahoe since 2021, when I first had the transmission replaced. Over the past 4 years, my truck has been in and out of the shop more than 20 times, each visit lasting 2 to 4 weeks. Despite all this, the transmission continued to slip while stopped and shift hard from 3rd to 2nd gear.
I was repeatedly told:

The torque converter was bad—it’s been replaced over 10 times.
The issue was due to bad mechanics, but I was assured a new tech would resolve it.
I dealt with 4 different individuals and multiple techs across both locations.

Three weeks ago, I dropped my truck off again and spoke with the person I’ve been working with for the past two years. After a week, I was told my vehicle had not been serviced properly under warranty. I was shocked—how could that be after so many visits and torque converter replacements? I was told it didn’t matter. After a 30-minute discussion, he agreed to fix the issue but said he wouldn’t make money from the repair and asked me to help pay. I refused, and he finally agreed to fix it—but said my warranty would be void.
I picked up my truck this past Saturday. I was told a mechanic would ride with me to confirm the fix—that didn’t happen. Then I was hit with a $510 charge for the TCM, which apparently wasn’t covered by the warranty. I asked to speak to the owner multiple times and was refused. I was told, “Don’t contact us again.”
To top it off, every time I picked up my truck, it was returned with an empty gas tank—even this last time. When I asked about it, I was told, “How did you think cars drive? They need gas.” Unbelievable.
I have messages and written statements backing up everything I’ve said, including one that reads:

“Wow, you’ve been very patient with us. I would probably handle things differently if I were in your shoes.”

I’ve tried to be respectful and patient. All I ever wanted was a properly functioning transmission—not 4 years of frustration and financial burden.
I wonder if the owner will reach out to discuss, if not.. oh well.. lesson learned from me.  Even though I was treated like trash, I won't lower my standards and mention all names that were involved.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Contradictory diagnoses repeated over many visits with no consistent explanation.

frontline_communication.snippet:
If I could give this place negative stars, I absolutely would. This April will mark 10 months since they have supposedly been “working” on my car, and the experience has been nothing short of frustrating and exhausting.

The first time I brought my car in for a transmission issue, the repair process seemed reasonable. I got the car back in about two weeks, and I was told the transmission replacement came with a warranty, which gave me some peace of mind. Unfortunately, that peace of mind didn’t last long. Within a month of getting my car back, the transmission started having problems again.

When I contacted them, they acknowledged the issue and assured me that they would honor the warranty and take care of the problem. Based on that promise, I brought the car back to them expecting a timely resolution. Instead, the situation has turned into a complete nightmare.

By April 2026, my car will have been sitting at their shop for 10 months. During that entire time, I have never once received a proactive update from them. Not a phone call, not a message, nothing. Every single time I want to know what’s going on with my vehicle, I have to be the one calling them. And when I do call, I’m given vague answers, excuses, or told something different each time. It feels like I’m constantly being sent in circles with no real progress or accountability.

The lack of communication is unacceptable. When someone leaves their vehicle with a shop, especially for something as serious as a transmission replacement, the least they should expect is honesty, updates, and a reasonable timeline. Instead, I’ve been left without my car for nearly a year while getting little to no clear information about what is actually being done.

At this point, the entire situation feels incredibly unprofessional and disrespectful to customers’ time and trust. I would strongly recommend that anyone considering bringing their vehicle here think twice. A warranty doesn’t mean much if the shop takes nearly a year to supposedly honor it and can’t even keep the customer informed.

This has been one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve ever had with an auto repair shop.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Vague and contradictory information given on every call.

frontline_communication.snippet:
On Monday, October 27, 2025, I visited Stereo Zone to purchase a camera to be installed in my car. Upon arrival, I purchased the camera for $303. I asked the owner how to delete old videos, and he told me that all recordings were stored on the SD card. I then asked how I could view the videos on my phone, and he said that it was only possible through the SD card.

After that, they installed the camera. At the end of the installation, one of the installers told me that I needed to download an app. This left me confused, as the owner had said that using a phone was not necessary to access the videos. The installers, however, insisted that I did need the app. They advised me to download it later and said they could not assist me at that moment because they were busy — even though I was the only customer in the store at the time.

When I arrived home, I downloaded the app, but it did not work. The next day, Tuesday, October 28, I called the store and explained that the equipment was not functioning properly. They told me to read the manual. I replied that this was difficult for me because English is not my first language. They then abruptly hung up on me.

On Wednesday, October 29, I went back to the store to resolve the issue. When I arrived, the store was closed. I returned the following day, October 30. Once again, no one in the store knew how to operate either the camera or the app. The owner repeated that the app was not required, while the installers insisted that it was. Eventually, one installer went with me to my car to demonstrate how the camera worked — but he clearly did not know how to use it either. Another installer joined us, told me once again to read the manual, and both of them walked away, saying they were going to call the owner. However, no one spoke to me again; they simply left me alone with a product that did not work for me.

I went back into the store and explained to the owner that the product he sold me was defective and that, since I had purchased it only four days earlier, I wanted to return it and receive a refund. He refused, stating that he had already told me the videos could be accessed directly through the SD card. I explained that his installers had told me otherwise — that I did need the app. He responded that the installers knew nothing about the product, then hebcompletely ignored me. I had no choice but to leave.

I would like to note that I am a woman and was alone during every visit. I am convinced that if I had been a man, I would not have been treated in the same manner. It is very clear to me that none of the employees — not even the owner — understand the product they sell, as each person gives different information. That is likely why they kept telling me to “read the manual.”

I also wish to warn others: do not trust the reviews you read about this store. They are clearly not genuine. A business that does not understand its own products and treats customers with such disrespect cannot possibly earn honest positive reviews. There are even reports that the owner himself writes fake reviews, asking customers for their phones so that he can write positive reviews on their behalf.

In the end, I went home with a product that does not work for me. I feel deceived and suffered a financial loss of $303. Please be cautious and avoid this establishment — they are not trustworthy.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Owner and installers gave contradictory information about whether the app was needed.

frontline_communication.snippet:
I had one of the most frustrating mechanic experiences at Lovefield Auto. I called ahead and spoke with Lloyd for 15 minutes, clearly explaining the issue—my 2020 Honda HR-V was diagnosed by the dealership with a bad right strut. He quoted me over $900 for the repair but said I had to wait a full week to bring the car in. Fine—I waited.

I dropped the car off promptly at 8AM. Radio silence until 2PM, when they finally said they test drove it but didn’t hear the sound. I told them: you have to turn the wheel—of course you won’t hear anything driving in a straight line. Two more hours passed. I had to call them back at 4:30PM for an update.

Then came the kicker: they told me they did finally hear the noise after turning the wheel—but said they weren’t sure what to do. Lloyd literally said they checked mechanic forums and Reddit and that fixing the strut might or might not solve the problem. A 50/50 chance, he said. They even mentioned it might be the shock, which doesn’t align at all with what I know or what the dealership diagnosed.

By 5PM (closing time), I was told the car “seems drivable” and that if the noise bothers me, I can come fix it—but they weren’t sure it would help. No confidence, no real diagnostic work, and zero follow-through. I felt completely brushed off and left with more questions than answers.

If you value your time, money, and peace of mind, go somewhere else. This shop wasted a week of my time and gave me nothing in return but confusion.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer left without updates and had to chase the shop, with no clear diagnostic explanation given.

​I brought my vehicle to this shop for standard emissions diagnostic service due to several existing fault codes. The initial agreement was to perform a proper diagnosis. I even agreed to leave the car overnight for them to properly identify the root cause.

​Within a couple of hours, I received a call that immediately raised red flags. They claimed they couldn't figure out the issue due to "too many codes," and stated they had to clear all the codes and then drive the car around to re-generate the data. Clearing the existing fault codes is the opposite of performing a diagnosis, as it erases the crucial historical data needed to track down intermittent issues.

This rendered the diagnostic service they agreed to completely useless.
​Skeptical of the process and unwilling to leave my car overnight given the incompetence shown, I retrieved the vehicle. Upon pickup, I was immediately presented with a bill for $128.75. When I objected, asking why I was paying for a diagnosis that was explicitly not performed (they had only cleared the codes), the mechanic offered vague and unprofessional justifications. He claimed they "fixed a loose hose"—an unapproved, minor action that did nothing to address the initial codes—and then launched into demanding payment, citing the need to "pay the workers."

I offer them to perform another diagnostic review so that it may give me at least some value out of the money that I'm spending. It for something unrelated issue like the AC noise and they said that will be an extra $160.

They did not give me the keys to my car untill I had paid. Needless to say completely unprofessional, scammy and avoid this mechanic at all costs.

frontline_communication.snippet: I would recommend Going to another diesel repair shop.   There is a strong lack of communication at this place   And they are  Fully competent when it comes to the trucks that their site says that they service.  I initially had an initial good experience at this place when I was first recommended by after that, it went quickly downhill   My last experience  Was I brought the truck into them for a rear door replacement.  We have a tight service schedule and we do not have a lot of trucks so we can’t afford a lot of downtime and I’ve spoke with the initial guy about doing it over the weekend because he said that they were open.  I also specified to the first guy that I was bringing it in for a door only and I do not need an oil change.  I had just put $300 worth of Titan additives into my engine To help stop the flow of the leaking oil .  Because this place did not have a good solution for the leaking oil  Without potentially thousands of dollars worth of repair and investigative problem-solving    Which tells me that they do not know that particular motor very well and I felt uncomfortable with them doing investigative Motor Repair if they did not have a clear picture of what was going wrong to start with .  That first weekend, one of my guys who was supposed to bring the truck in did not end up making it in    So I called back the next week and let them know that we will be bringing it in this weekend .  I did not go into further explanation on what it was going to be serviced on this truck because that full detail was covered from the previous week    When we went to go pick the truck up on Monday morning   We were shocked to find the backdoor still in the state of disrepair that we left it   And that they had done the oil change that was specifically requested not to be done.  When I have confronted the shop about this issue   They said they were not going to charge me for the oil change, but they declined to do any further business.  Piss poor way to handle business in Dallas Fort Worth if you want to maintain a reputation.  My strong recommendation if you have an Isuzu diesel box truck   Is that you take it to industrial power  Or anywhere else because of my experience on how they treat you, you will end up spending way more money and not getting your problem solved
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer explicitly instructed no oil change yet they performed it and ignored the door request.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I’ve been dealing with transmission issues on my 2015 Chevy Tahoe since 2021, when I first had the transmission replaced. Over the past 4 years, my truck has been in and out of the shop more than 20 times, each visit lasting 2 to 4 weeks. Despite all this, the transmission continued to slip while stopped and shift hard from 3rd to 2nd gear.
I was repeatedly told:

The torque converter was bad—it’s been replaced over 10 times.
The issue was due to bad mechanics, but I was assured a new tech would resolve it.
I dealt with 4 different individuals and multiple techs across both locations.

Three weeks ago, I dropped my truck off again and spoke with the person I’ve been working with for the past two years. After a week, I was told my vehicle had not been serviced properly under warranty. I was shocked—how could that be after so many visits and torque converter replacements? I was told it didn’t matter. After a 30-minute discussion, he agreed to fix the issue but said he wouldn’t make money from the repair and asked me to help pay. I refused, and he finally agreed to fix it—but said my warranty would be void.
I picked up my truck this past Saturday. I was told a mechanic would ride with me to confirm the fix—that didn’t happen. Then I was hit with a $510 charge for the TCM, which apparently wasn’t covered by the warranty. I asked to speak to the owner multiple times and was refused. I was told, “Don’t contact us again.”
To top it off, every time I picked up my truck, it was returned with an empty gas tank—even this last time. When I asked about it, I was told, “How did you think cars drive? They need gas.” Unbelievable.
I have messages and written statements backing up everything I’ve said, including one that reads:

“Wow, you’ve been very patient with us. I would probably handle things differently if I were in your shoes.”

I’ve tried to be respectful and patient. All I ever wanted was a properly functioning transmission—not 4 years of frustration and financial burden.

frontline_communication.snippet:
I’ve been dealing with transmission issues on my 2015 Chevy Tahoe since 2021, when I first had the transmission replaced. Over the past 4 years, my truck has been in and out of the shop more than 20 times, each visit lasting 2 to 4 weeks. Despite all this, the transmission continued to slip while stopped and shift hard from 3rd to 2nd gear.
I was repeatedly told:

The torque converter was bad—it’s been replaced over 10 times.
The issue was due to bad mechanics, but I was assured a new tech would resolve it.
I dealt with 4 different individuals and multiple techs across both locations.

Three weeks ago, I dropped my truck off again and spoke with the person I’ve been working with for the past two years. After a week, I was told my vehicle had not been serviced properly under warranty. I was shocked—how could that be after so many visits and torque converter replacements? I was told it didn’t matter. After a 30-minute discussion, he agreed to fix the issue but said he wouldn’t make money from the repair and asked me to help pay. I refused, and he finally agreed to fix it—but said my warranty would be void.
I picked up my truck this past Saturday. I was told a mechanic would ride with me to confirm the fix—that didn’t happen. Then I was hit with a $510 charge for the TCM, which apparently wasn’t covered by the warranty. I asked to speak to the owner multiple times and was refused. I was told, “Don’t contact us again.”
To top it off, every time I picked up my truck, it was returned with an empty gas tank—even this last time. When I asked about it, I was told, “How did you think cars drive? They need gas.” Unbelievable.
I have messages and written statements backing up everything I’ve said, including one that reads:

“Wow, you’ve been very patient with us. I would probably handle things differently if I were in your shoes.”

I’ve tried to be respectful and patient. All I ever wanted was a properly functioning transmission—not 4 years of frustration and financial burden.
I wonder if the owner will reach out to discuss, if not.. oh well.. lesson learned from me. Even though I was treated like trash, I won't lower my standards and mention all names that were involved.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Dismissive, mocking tone from staff when the customer raised a legitimate concern.

frontline_communication.snippet: I was very disappointed in the work done on my car by Tin Lizzie.  They installed custom carpet in my 1972 Alfa Romeo GTV, and it ended up costing me a fair amount of money and frustration to fix things they broke.  The worst issue was they screwed a large screw completely through the wiring harness that runs to the rear of the vehicle -- I don't know if they could have hit it more dead center if they tried.  At that point, they should have realized something was wrong because the car no longer ran because the electric fuel pump wire was in that harness.  Even worse, they didn't bother to tell me that the car wasn't running until several weeks later when I arrived to pick the car up!  It's a good thing I had a trailer and didn't plan to drive it home!  I ended up taking the car to an Italian car specialist to diagnose and fix the electrical problems caused by the short circuit and damaged wire, and that really put me behind the 8 ball as I'm trying to get this car finished.  Also, the car was promised to be done three times; the first two times it wasn't ready.  Usually that's not a big deal, but I'm active duty Army and live out of state (and they know this), so I burned up leave unnecessarily because the car wasn't ready when they said it would be, and I had already taken leave.  They also had trouble with seemingly simple tasks, like removing seats and removing a bolt-in rollcage.  The communication was also very limited; in the several months that they had the car, I think they may have called once with an update or a question.  Otherwise, I had to call them every week to find out what was happening.  Sorry for writing a book, but I waited for a few months after getting the car back to write this review and I've calmed down considerably.  I also generally don't leave negative reviews, but I just didn't feel right not giving potential customers some feedback on my experience.  In closing, I will say that Lucinda and Joel are both kind and cordial, their prices are reasonable, and I wish them the best of luck moving forward.  However, I also hope they learned from the mistakes made on my car.  Scott Walters
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer received almost no updates and had to chase the shop weekly for information.
